```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath("..", mustWork = TRUE))
```

```{r publication-figures, message=FALSE}

# ============================================================
# ICIT 2027 - PUBLICATION QUALITY FIGURES
# Five CSV files | Five scientific figures
# Author: Umar Aziz
#
# Output: PDF, PNG (600 dpi), TIFF (600 dpi)
#
# Statistical integrity:
# No recomputation of means, confidence intervals or q-values.
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# 0. INSTALL AND LOAD PACKAGES
# ============================================================

packages <- c(
  "readr",
  "dplyr",
  "tidyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "patchwork",
  "scales"
)

missing_packages <- packages[
  !packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Install these R packages before rendering: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}

invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE))


# ============================================================
# 1. WORKING DIRECTORY
# ============================================================

data_dir <- getwd()

output_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "generated-figures")

dir.create(
  output_dir,
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)


# ============================================================
# 2. IMPORT ORIGINAL CSV FILES
# ============================================================

g1 <- read_csv(
  "Graph_1_Baseline_Validation.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

g2 <- read_csv(
  "Graph_2_Accuracy_vs_Packet_Loss.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

g3 <- read_csv(
  "Graph_3_Weighted_Drift_Improvement.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

g4 <- read_csv(
  "Graph_4_Accuracy_Freshness_Communication.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

g5 <- read_csv(
  "Graph_5_Deadline_Freshness_Violations.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# 3. GLOBAL DESIGN SETTINGS
# ============================================================

# Publication color palette
COL_NAVY   <- "#17365D"
COL_BLUE   <- "#0072B2"
COL_ORANGE <- "#D55E00"
COL_GREEN  <- "#009E73"
COL_PURPLE <- "#984EA3"
COL_GREY   <- "#666666"

# Estimator palette
estimator_colors <- c(
  "Hold" = COL_BLUE,
  "Weighted drift" = COL_ORANGE,
  "Local linear" = COL_GREEN,
  "Full drift" = COL_PURPLE
)

# Feedback palette
feedback_colors <- c(
  "ACK" = COL_BLUE,
  "No-ACK" = COL_ORANGE
)

# Deadline palette
deadline_colors <- c(
  "2x" = COL_BLUE,
  "3x" = COL_ORANGE,
  "6x" = COL_GREEN
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication theme
# ------------------------------------------------------------

theme_publication <- function(base_size = 11) {

  theme_classic(
    base_size = base_size,
    base_family = "sans"
  ) +

    theme(

      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 13,
        color = "#202020",
        margin = margin(b = 8)
      ),

      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 10,
        color = COL_GREY
      ),

      axis.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 10.5,
        color = "#202020"
      ),

      axis.text = element_text(
        size = 9,
        color = "#303030"
      ),

      axis.line = element_line(
        color = "#444444",
        linewidth = 0.4
      ),

      axis.ticks = element_line(
        color = "#444444",
        linewidth = 0.35
      ),

      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        color = "#EAEAEA",
        linewidth = 0.3
      ),

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

      panel.background = element_rect(
        fill = "white",
        color = NA
      ),

      plot.background = element_rect(
        fill = "white",
        color = NA
      ),

      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "#F2F4F7",
        color = "#DDDDDD",
        linewidth = 0.4
      ),

      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 9
      ),

      legend.position = "bottom",

      legend.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 9
      ),

      legend.text = element_text(
        size = 9
      ),

      legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.3, "cm"),

      panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.9, "lines"),

      plot.margin = margin(12, 14, 12, 12)
    )
}


# ============================================================
# 4. HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================

# Consistent signal labels
signal_name <- function(x) {
  recode(
    x,
    "Temp" = "Temperature",
    "Moist" = "Soil moisture"
  )
}

# Consistent feedback labels
feedback_name <- function(x) {
  recode(
    x,
    "ack" = "ACK",
    "no_ack" = "No-ACK"
  )
}

# Consistent estimator labels
estimator_name <- function(x) {
  recode(
    x,
    "hold" = "Hold",
    "weighted_drift" = "Weighted drift",
    "local_linear" = "Local linear",
    "full_drift" = "Full drift"
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Export helper
# ------------------------------------------------------------

save_figure <- function(plot, filename,
                        width = 10, height = 7) {

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(filename, ".pdf")
    ),
    plot = plot,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    device = cairo_pdf,
    bg = "white"
  )

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(filename, ".png")
    ),
    plot = plot,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    dpi = 600,
    bg = "white"
  )

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(filename, ".tiff")
    ),
    plot = plot,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    dpi = 600,
    compression = "lzw",
    bg = "white"
  )

  message("Saved: ", filename)
}


# ============================================================
# GRAPH 1 - BASELINE VALIDATION
# ============================================================

# Convert to long format for three matched panels.
# Original values remain unchanged.

g1_sim <- g1 %>%
  select(
    threshold,
    update_rate,
    mean_aoi,
    mse
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -threshold,
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(type = "Simulation")


g1_theory <- g1 %>%
  select(
    threshold,
    theoretical_update_rate,
    theoretical_mean_aoi,
    theoretical_mse
  ) %>%
  rename(
    update_rate = theoretical_update_rate,
    mean_aoi = theoretical_mean_aoi,
    mse = theoretical_mse
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -threshold,
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(type = "Theory")


g1_plot <- bind_rows(
  g1_sim,
  g1_theory
) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c("update_rate", "mean_aoi", "mse"),
      labels = c(
        "A  Update rate",
        "B  Mean AoI",
        "C  Mean squared error"
      )
    )
  )


graph1 <- ggplot(
  g1_plot,
  aes(x = threshold, y = value)
) +

  geom_line(
    data = filter(g1_plot, type == "Theory"),
    aes(group = 1, linetype = type),
    color = COL_GREY,
    linewidth = 0.85
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = filter(g1_plot, type == "Simulation"),
    aes(color = type),
    size = 2.7
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~metric,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Simulation" = COL_BLUE)
  ) +

  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("Theory" = "dashed")
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(g1$threshold))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Threshold",
    y = "Metric value",
    color = NULL,
    linetype = NULL
  ) +

  theme_publication() +

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )


print(graph1)

save_figure(
  graph1,
  "Graph_1_Baseline_Validation",
  width = 11.5,
  height = 4.0
)


# ============================================================
# GRAPH 2 - ACCURACY VS PACKET LOSS
# ============================================================

# Use threshold_multiplier = 1.0.
# This avoids mixing different threshold settings.
# All original means and CI values are retained.

selected_threshold <- 1.0

g2_plot <- g2 %>%

  filter(
    near(threshold_multiplier, selected_threshold)
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    loss_percent = loss_probability * 100,

    Signal = signal_name(signal),

    Feedback = feedback_name(feedback_model),

    Estimator = estimator_name(estimator),

    Estimator = factor(
      Estimator,
      levels = names(estimator_colors)
    ),

    Feedback = factor(
      Feedback,
      levels = c("ACK", "No-ACK")
    ),

    Signal = factor(
      Signal,
      levels = c("Temperature", "Soil moisture")
    )
  )


graph2 <- ggplot(
  g2_plot,
  aes(
    x = loss_percent,
    y = mse_mean,
    color = Estimator,
    group = Estimator
  )
) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.85
  ) +

  geom_point(
    size = 2.1
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mse_ci_low,
      ymax = mse_ci_high
    ),
    width = 1.2,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Signal ~ Feedback,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = estimator_colors
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 50, by = 10),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.04))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.01)
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Packet loss probability (%)",
    y = "Mean squared error (MSE)",
    color = "Estimator"
  ) +

  theme_publication()


print(graph2)

save_figure(
  graph2,
  "Graph_2_Accuracy_vs_Packet_Loss",
  width = 10.5,
  height = 7.5
)


# ============================================================
# GRAPH 3 - WEIGHTED-DRIFT IMPROVEMENT
# ============================================================

# Positive improvement = weighted drift performs better
# than hold, according to the saved CSV definition.
#
# Significance uses ORIGINAL BH-adjusted q-values.
# No p-values or q-values are recalculated.

g3_plot <- g3 %>%

  mutate(
    loss_percent = loss_probability * 100,

    Signal = signal_name(signal),

    Feedback = feedback_name(feedback_model),

    significance = ifelse(
      !is.na(q_value) & q_value < 0.05,
      "*",
      ""
    ),

    Signal = factor(
      Signal,
      levels = c("Temperature", "Soil moisture")
    ),

    Feedback = factor(
      Feedback,
      levels = c("ACK", "No-ACK")
    )
  )


# Symmetric limits, ensuring that zero is at the
# center of the color scale.

heat_limit <- max(
  abs(g3_plot$aggregate_relative_improvement_percent),
  na.rm = TRUE
)


graph3 <- ggplot(
  g3_plot,
  aes(
    x = factor(loss_percent),
    y = factor(threshold_multiplier),
    fill = aggregate_relative_improvement_percent
  )
) +

  geom_tile(
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.65
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(label = significance),
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#111111",
    size = 5.2
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Signal ~ Feedback
  ) +

  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#B2182B",
    mid = "#FFFFFF",
    high = "#2166AC",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-heat_limit, heat_limit),
    name = "Relative MSE\nimprovement (%)"
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Packet loss probability (%)",
    y = "Threshold multiplier"
  ) +

  theme_publication() +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.1, "lines"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )


print(graph3)

save_figure(
  graph3,
  "Graph_3_Weighted_Drift_Improvement",
  width = 10,
  height = 7.2
)


# ============================================================
# GRAPH 4 - ACCURACY, FRESHNESS, COMMUNICATION
# ============================================================

# All loss probabilities are retained.
# Points are connected in THRESHOLD ORDER.
#
# geom_path() is intentionally used instead of
# geom_line(), because geom_line() sorts by x.
#
# Upper: MSE (Hold and Weighted drift)
# Lower: AoI (Hold only, avoiding duplicate values)


g4_plot <- g4 %>%
  mutate(
    Signal = signal_name(signal),

    Feedback = feedback_name(feedback_model),

    Estimator = estimator_name(estimator),

    Loss = factor(
      paste0(
        round(loss_probability * 100),
        "% loss"
      ),
      levels = paste0(
        round(sort(unique(g4$loss_probability)) * 100),
        "% loss"
      )
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Upper panels: accuracy
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g4_mse_data <- g4_plot %>%

  arrange(
    Signal,
    Loss,
    Feedback,
    Estimator,
    threshold_multiplier
  )


g4_mse <- ggplot(
  g4_mse_data,
  aes(
    x = attempted_update_rate_per_minute_mean,
    y = mse_mean,
    color = Feedback,
    linetype = Estimator,
    group = interaction(
      Signal,
      Loss,
      Feedback,
      Estimator
    )
  )
) +

  geom_path(
    linewidth = 0.75
  ) +

  geom_point(
    size = 1.55
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Signal ~ Loss,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = feedback_colors
  ) +

  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Hold" = "solid",
      "Weighted drift" = "dashed"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "A  Estimation accuracy",
    x = "Attempted updates (packets/min)",
    y = "Mean squared error",
    color = "Feedback",
    linetype = "Estimator"
  ) +

  theme_publication(base_size = 10) +

  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 40,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Lower panels: freshness
# IMPORTANT: hold only
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g4_aoi_data <- g4_plot %>%

  filter(estimator == "hold") %>%

  arrange(
    Signal,
    Loss,
    Feedback,
    threshold_multiplier
  )


g4_aoi <- ggplot(
  g4_aoi_data,
  aes(
    x = attempted_update_rate_per_minute_mean,
    y = mean_aoi_minutes_mean,
    color = Feedback,
    group = interaction(
      Signal,
      Loss,
      Feedback
    )
  )
) +

  geom_path(
    linewidth = 0.75
  ) +

  geom_point(
    size = 1.55
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Signal ~ Loss,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = feedback_colors
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "B  Information freshness",
    x = "Attempted updates (packets/min)",
    y = "Mean AoI (minutes)",
    color = "Feedback"
  ) +

  theme_publication(base_size = 10) +

  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 40,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine accuracy and freshness vertically
# ------------------------------------------------------------

graph4 <- (
  g4_mse / g4_aoi
) +

  plot_layout(
    heights = c(1, 1),
    guides = "collect"
  ) &

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )


print(graph4)

save_figure(
  graph4,
  "Graph_4_Accuracy_Freshness_Communication",
  width = 17,
  height = 10.5
)


# ============================================================
# GRAPH 5 - DEADLINE FRESHNESS VIOLATIONS
# ============================================================

# Select threshold_multiplier = 1.0
# Keep three deadline multipliers: 2, 3 and 6.
#
# Original CIs are multiplied by 100 for plotting.
# No confidence interval is recomputed.

g5_plot <- g5 %>%

  filter(
    near(threshold_multiplier, selected_threshold),
    freshness_deadline_multiplier %in% c(2, 3, 6)
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    loss_percent = loss_probability * 100,

    violation_percent =
      freshness_violation_rate_mean * 100,

    violation_ci_low =
      freshness_violation_rate_ci_low * 100,

    violation_ci_high =
      freshness_violation_rate_ci_high * 100,

    Signal = signal_name(signal),

    Feedback = feedback_name(feedback_model),

    Deadline = factor(
      freshness_deadline_multiplier,
      levels = c(2, 3, 6),
      labels = c("2x", "3x", "6x")
    ),

    Signal = factor(
      Signal,
      levels = c("Temperature", "Soil moisture")
    ),

    Feedback = factor(
      Feedback,
      levels = c("ACK", "No-ACK")
    )
  )


graph5 <- ggplot(
  g5_plot,
  aes(
    x = loss_percent,
    y = violation_percent,
    color = Deadline,
    group = Deadline
  )
) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +

  geom_point(
    size = 2.1
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = violation_ci_low,
      ymax = violation_ci_high
    ),
    width = 1.1,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Signal ~ Feedback
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = deadline_colors
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 50, by = 10)
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 100)
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Packet loss probability (%)",
    y = "Freshness violation rate (%)",
    color = "Deadline multiplier"
  ) +

  theme_publication()


print(graph5)

save_figure(
  graph5,
  "Graph_5_Deadline_Freshness_Violations",
  width = 10.5,
  height = 7.5
)


# ============================================================
# 5. FINAL VERIFICATION
# ============================================================

cat("\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("PUBLICATION FIGURES COMPLETED\n")
cat("========================================\n")

cat("\nWorking directory:\n")
cat(data_dir, "\n")

cat("\nOutput directory:\n")
cat(output_dir, "\n")

cat("\nOriginal rows loaded:\n")
cat("Graph 1:", nrow(g1), "\n")
cat("Graph 2:", nrow(g2), "\n")
cat("Graph 3:", nrow(g3), "\n")
cat("Graph 4:", nrow(g4), "\n")
cat("Graph 5:", nrow(g5), "\n")

cat("\nPlot rows used:\n")
cat("Graph 2:", nrow(g2_plot), "\n")
cat("Graph 3:", nrow(g3_plot), "\n")
cat("Graph 4 MSE:", nrow(g4_mse_data), "\n")
cat("Graph 4 AoI:", nrow(g4_aoi_data), "\n")
cat("Graph 5:", nrow(g5_plot), "\n")

cat("\nFiles created:\n")

print(
  list.files(
    output_dir,
    pattern = "\\.(pdf|png|tiff)$",
    full.names = FALSE
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat("All original statistical values preserved.\n")
cat("No confidence intervals recalculated.\n")
cat("No adjusted p-values recalculated.\n")
cat("========================================\n")

```
